abstract: Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is a multidomain signaling protein implicated in Parkinson's disease whose activity is closely linked to conformational state. How these structural transitions shape the cellular molecular environment of LRRK2 remains poorly understood. Here, we combined nanobody-mediated conformational control with miniTurbo proximity proteomics to define molecular neighborhoods associated with inhibitory, neutral, and activating LRRK2 states. Structural modeling suggested that the activating nanobody Nb22 targets the WD40 domain and destabilizes interactions maintaining the autoinhibited conformation. Consistent with this model, activation was accompanied by ordered, reciprocal remodeling of the LRRK2 proximity proteome, with progressive enrichment of centrosomal, ciliary, and RAB/endolysosomal machinery and depletion of soluble cytosolic, proteostasis-associated and 14-3-3 proteins. Notably, the Nb22-associated proteome combined centrosomal and endolysosomal components previously linked to distinct LRRK2 signaling environments. These findings support a model in which conformational transitions reorganize the spatial molecular neighborhood of LRRK2 and thereby couple kinase state to distinct cellular signaling networks.
